findings.text: the early return that keeps a main checkout's own git directory out of the write roots has no test that reddens if the guard is removed: both tests compose a fence for a linked worktree, where the worktree git directory differs from the common directory, so deleting the guard changes nothing the suite executes while reckon/_backends.py:2111 and the evidence record both state the refusal as a guarantee.

item_verdicts.diff: read both commits against base f01992d3; a13d1cc2 is the production helper plus one call line plus the new test file, 5f6e9ff8 is the plan landing record, the evidence anchor and four logs plus a figure, 516 insertions and one deletion, all inside the declared scope.
item_verdicts.done_when: the done_when names tests/test_a_fenced_worker_can_commit.py executed under a real bubblewrap fence with a commit-reachability check, three refusal probes, a stated skip reason and a logged negative control; the manifest records that gate at head a13d1cc2 (27 passed) against base f01992d3 (25 passed, zero added) and I re-ran the named file at the reviewed head 5f6e9ff8, 2 passed, in the run-dir log recheck-fenced-commit.txt.
item_verdicts.goal: the goal asks that a fenced worker's own worktree git directory and its repository's shared object store become writable while the rest of the sealed checkout stays read-only; reckon/_backends.py:2111 worktree_git_write_roots resolves exactly those two paths and reckon/_backends.py:2199 adds them to the write roots, and nothing else below the sealed main checkout is granted.
item_verdicts.manifest: read; it records the gate result, the base arm, the lint delta, the negative control and the evidence anchor, and its follow_ons names the unmeasured auto-gc residual rather than claiming it away.
item_verdicts.write_paths: the manifest declares five write paths and every path the two commits touch lies inside them, with no file the goal does not imply.

justifications.durability: tests/test_a_fenced_worker_can_commit.py:206 is an executed negative control that reddens on the exact regression — with the two roots withheld the commit fails with a read-only file system — but the main-checkout branch at reckon/_backends.py:2148 has no test that reddens if the guard is deleted.
justifications.evidence: every done_when item has a receipt on disk (docs/figures/a-worker-cannot-write-your-home/gate-git-roots-head.txt, its base arm and negative-control-git-roots.txt) and my recheck at the reviewed head passed 2/2, with only tests/test_a_fenced_worker_can_commit.py:65 suppressing auto-gc so the production command's gc path stays unmeasured.
justifications.fit: the helper sits beside the module's other fence helpers and follows their Path and subprocess idiom, the test reuses the sibling fence files' __main__ red-log pattern, and lint over the touched paths is unchanged.
justifications.goal_fidelity: reckon/_backends.py:2199 adds both roots to the write roots and the executed probe at tests/test_a_fenced_worker_can_commit.py:167 shows the commit landing while the main index, refs/heads and working tree each stay refused.
justifications.scope_discipline: every path in the two commits lies inside the manifest's declared write paths, and the docs edits are the landing record and evidence the dispatch's landing contract requires.
